children: , the database and AI cloud provider, faces a tougher market for funding its AI buildout. Shares fell nearly 7% to $134.605 at 10.28am ET time on Thursday morning. Investors want cloud growth, but they are watching what it costs Oracle to deliver it.

The gap is getting harder to ignore. Reuters reported that AI related issuers' bonds traded about 115 basis points above benchmarks, versus 78 basis points for the broader investment grade market. That 37 basis point difference is a market average, not Oracle's borrowing rate. Oracle, meanwhile, reported $11.6 billion in quarterly cloud revenue, up 62%. Demand is racing ahead; building the capacity to serve it still takes cash.

The valuation picture adds another wrinkle. At $134.605, Oracle trades 30.07% below the $192.48 GF Value shown in the picture. That gap may catch a bargain hunter's eye, but the next test is practical: can Oracle turn its cloud contracts into cash quickly enough to support the buildout without making financing more expensive?

title: Oracle Drops 7% as AI Debt Carries a Wider Spread
